subject: SAC-B2 caller-owned feature-family localized competition

biological_reference.citation: Amin et al. (2020), Localized inhibition in the Drosophila mushroom body, eLife 9:e56954
biological_reference.engineering_reading: Local inhibition is stronger nearby but not perfectly isolated; evaluate family-local winner budgets together with a bounded global residual path rather than assuming hard partitions.

invariants: family mapping is owned by the SUI adapter, not SACS Core
kind receives no reserved local budget in these fixtures
total reserved local plus global residual budget does not exceed Sparse.Active
absent-family budget is not automatically redistributed
merged signatures are sorted and duplicate dimensions are collapsed

syntheticFixtures.observation: Both localized policies recover the structurally aligned candidate that global k-WTA loses to text-cardinality domination.
Hard equal family reservation reverses a correct global ordering toward a narrow-family match; retaining half of the budget as global residual restores the broad-evidence candidate in this fixture.

initialNaiveReconstruction.note: A standalone Go reconstruction created new sparse Encoder scratch arrays for every family and item.

requestScopedEncoderReuseReconstruction.note: The branch implementation was revised to reuse one sparse Encoder per distinct active width within a request. This standalone reconstruction mirrors that lifecycle but is not an exact repository checkout.
requestScopedEncoderReuseReconstruction.interpretation: Encoder reuse removes most of the naive setup cost, but localized competition remains materially more expensive than the global baseline and needs further allocation work before any production consideration.

localVerification.method: Standalone deterministic Go reconstruction of the current sparse encoder, SUI feature projection, family mapping, local winner budgets, signature merge, and request-scoped encoder reuse.
